title: Boston has one of the best wine bars, wine shops in America, according to USA Today readers
author: Kristi Palma
bullets: Gray's Hall in South Boston ranked No. 10 best wine bar in USA Today's 10Best Readers' Choice Awards.
Neighborhood Wines in Boston placed No. 10 among the best wine shops in USA Today's 10Best Readers' Choice Awards.
1010 Wine & Events in Inglewood, Calif., and Perry’s Fine Wines & Liquors in Palm Springs, Calif., ranked No. 1.

title: Newton police searching for girl, 14, who disappeared from DCF custody
author: Elizabeth Mehler
bullets: Newton police are searching for 14-year-old Daiyanaliz Diaz who left DCF custody at Newton Wellesley Hospital on July 3.
Diaz is described as a dark-skinned Hispanic female, 5'3", wearing a black tank top, grey shorts, and black sneakers.
Authorities urge those with information on Diaz's whereabouts to contact Newton Police at 617-796-2123 or DCF at 781-641-8500.

title: Livestream: Lindsay Clancy murder trial resumes after jurors hear her emotional journal entries
author: Abby Patkin
bullets: Lindsay Clancy stands trial for the murder of her three children in Duxbury, charged with first-degree murder.
Clancy claims an insanity defense, citing postpartum mental illness, while prosecutors argue her actions were deliberate.
Jurors reviewed Clancy's emotional journal entries detailing her mental health struggles and heard testimony on postpartum psychosis.

title: Adley Rutschman trade grades: Did Boston overpay for All-Star catcher?
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Boston Red Sox acquired All-Star catcher Adley Rutschman from Baltimore Orioles, upgrading their catching corps.
The Red Sox traded Carlos Narvaez and prospects Anthony Eyanson, Kyson Witherspoon, Enddy Azocar, and a player to be named later.
Experts graded the trade from A to C+, citing potential long-term risk due to high-profile prospects traded away.

title: Here’s how much an associate professor makes in Boston
author: Annie Jonas
bullets: Retired associate professor Jay earned $172,000 annually, working hybrid at Northeastern University's Boston campus.
His major monthly expense is $4,200 towards roughly $500,000 in family student loans.
Post-retirement, Jay supplements income by teaching part-time, earning $18,000 annually from two courses at Northeastern.

title: Cambridge City Council votes to temporarily restore controversial ShotSpotter gunshot detection technology
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Cambridge City Council voted 6-3 to temporarily restore ShotSpotter gunshot detection technology in areas it was previously used.
The system's reinstatement follows a July 4 shooting incident and aims to assess community input on its use.
The resident assembly will review ShotSpotter's effectiveness over 90 days, with council revisiting the issue afterward.

title: 4 takeaways from Craig Breslow’s Red Sox trade-deadline press conference
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Red Sox acquired catcher Adley Rutschman from Orioles, trading Carlos Narvaez, Anthony Eyanson, and others.
Marcelo Mayer was traded to the Giants for reliever Erik Miller, impacting Boston's infield prospects.
Boston foresees Franklin Arias as a future shortstop, possibly debuting in the majors this fall.

title: ‘Playbook of destruction’: Markey, Moulton meet for combative second debate ahead of Sept. primary
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Sen. Ed Markey and Rep. Seth Moulton engaged in a combative second primary debate, focusing on generational change and policy differences.
Both candidates accused each other of supporting Middle East wars, with Markey criticizing Moulton's defense votes and Moulton criticizing Markey's Iraq war vote.
Markey and Moulton both claimed the progressive label, despite policy differences; Markey criticized Moulton over past comments about transgender athletes.

title: 4 unproven Patriots players who are standing out at training camp
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Eli Raridon and Tanner Arkin are emerging TE talents for the Patriots during training camp.
Karon Prunty, a fifth-round pick, is gaining valuable reps in the Patriots' secondary in Foxborough.
Undrafted rookie Khalil Jacobs is impressing as a versatile LB option on New England's depth chart.

title: After jokes on GBH, state senator says agritourism like corn mazes are serious business
author: Ross Cristantiello
bullets: Massachusetts Senator Jo Comerford advocates for a $5 million agritourism amendment in the economic bill 'fun agenda'.
Comerford criticizes GBH hosts for trivializing agritourism, stressing its importance for struggling Massachusetts farmers.
Massachusetts lost 27,000 acres of farmland from 2017 to 2022, prompting efforts to boost agritourism as economic relief.
